extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students and instructors learning or teaching introductory mathematical proofs
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook introducing standard methods of proving mathematical theorems, with chapters on sets, logic, counting, proof techniques, relations, functions, cardinality, and related topics; intended for use in undergraduate courses and self-study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stated purpose / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: This book is an introduction to the standard methods of proving mathematical theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the intended level and focus (introductory coverage of proof techniques). Useful for deciding appropriateness for courses or self-study; the Contents list details specific topics covered (parts I–IV and chapters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents / Topics covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Contents include: Part I: Fundamentals (Sets, Logic, Counting), Part II: How to Prove Conditional Statements (Direct Proof, Contrapositive, Contradiction), Part III: More on Proof (If-and-Only-If, Existence/Uniqueness, Induction, Disproof), Part IV: Relations, Functions and Cardinality (Relations, Functions, Proofs in Calculus, Cardinality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The detailed chapter and subsection list defines the curriculum and learning objectives; instructors can map chapters to course modules. The Contents also indicate presence of examples (e.g., Fermat/Perfect Numbers, Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, Fibonacci Numbers) and exercises with solutions (see 'Solutions').

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability / distribution options
rubrics_metrics.description: You can order a copy through Barnes & Noble or Amazon. You can also download a free PDF version HERE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical copies (paperback/hardcover with ISBNs/prices) and a free PDF are both available; distribution by Ingram is noted for bookstore orders (see 'Note to adopters').

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption / instructor guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Note to adopters: Your bookstore will need to know that the book is distributed by Ingram. Please let me know if you use Book of Proof in your classes and I will update the adoptions list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural guidance for instructors adopting the book: inform bookstores about the distributor and notify the author so the adoptions list can be maintained. Implies author support for instructors and tracking of course adoptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary materials and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: An adoptions list is here, and ancillary materials are here. See also the Translations Page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of ancillary materials and translations suggests supplemental resources (e.g., instructor resources, translated editions) that support teaching and use; links are provided on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions availability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A solutions section exists (beginning at page 292), which is relevant for instructors and learners checking answers; may include worked solutions for exercises in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement / approval
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been approved by the American Institute of Mathematics' Open Textbook Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An external endorsement indicating suitability as an open textbook; may factor into adoption decisions or perceived quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning / errata policy
rubrics_metrics.description: On February 5, 2025 I issued edition 3.4 in print and PDF (ISBN's unchanged). This slight revision corrects a handful of typos found by readers. All orders printed after February 5 will be edition 3.4. I incorporate reader feedback in periodic revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author updates and minor revisions are issued to correct mistakes; readers/instructors should check edition numbers and errata when adopting or citing the text.
